literal: Even if they live than the celestials, those who fear the bamboo-resembling shoulders of their wife indeed have no dignity.
translation: Even if they live with the splendor of the immortal gods, those who live in fear of their wife's bamboo-like shoulders possess no true dignity.
modern: மனைவியின் மூங்கில் போன்ற தோள்களுக்கு அஞ்சி வாழ்பவர்கள், தேவர்களைப் போல வாழ்ந்தாலும் பெருமை இல்லாதவர்களே ஆவர்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the loss of honor for men who are overly submissive to their wives. The poet uses the classical metaphor of 'bamboo-like shoulders' (அமையார்தோள்) to describe the wife, representing her beauty and feminine grace. A husband who fears his wife instead of leading with mutual respect loses his dignity (பாடு). Even if such men enjoy a life of supreme comfort and longevity like the immortal gods (இமையார்), they are deemed completely devoid of greatness.
